issues.claim: ICMR STW AKI 2026: 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate over 2–5 min under ECG (up to 3 times), nebulised salbutamol 10 mg, insulin 10 U with dextrose. See the Hyperkalaemia protocol.
issues.problem: The insulin–dextrose dose is incomplete. The line leaves out how much dextrose the source gives with 10 U insulin, which is what prevents hypoglycaemia, so a reader cannot give the sourced regimen from this line. Every other number in the line matches the source.
issues.correction: ICMR STW AKI 2026: 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate over 2–5 min slow IV under ECG monitoring (can be repeated up to 3 times), inhaled salbutamol 10 mg, insulin 10 U in 50 mL of 50% dextrose or 100 mL of 25% dextrose. See the Hyperkalaemia protocol.
issues.evidence: ICMR STW Acute Kidney Injury (updated July 2026), box 'TREATMENT OF HYPERKALEMIA': '• 10 ml of 10% calcium gluconate over 2-5 minutes slow IV under ECG monitoring, can be repeated upto 3 times • Inhaled Salbutamol : 10mg (4 respules of 2.5ml Salbutamol) • Insulin-dextrose: 10U in 50ml of 50% dextrose or 100ml of 25% dextrose' — https://www.icmr.gov.in/icmrobject/uploads/STWs/1784807239_acutekidneyinjury-updated.pdf

issues.step: Crush in disasters: fasciotomy, amputation, infection
issues.claim: Sever 2023: not routine in disasters — only when clearly indicated (absent distal pulses from compression, disproportionate pain, radical debridement) or pressures 30–40 mm Hg not falling over 6 h.
issues.problem: The line turns a qualifier into a required condition. Sever 2023 gives compartment pressures in the 30–40 mm Hg range as the objective criterion, 'especially if' they show no fall over 6 h. As written, a clinician could think they must watch 6 h of non-falling pressures before decompressing, which conflicts with the next point ('operate as soon as possible'). The protocol's own note already uses the correct 'especially'.
issues.correction: Sever 2023: not routine in disasters — only when clearly indicated (absent distal pulses from compression, disproportionate pain, radical debridement) or compartment pressures of 30–40 mm Hg, especially if not falling over 6 h.
issues.evidence: Sever MS et al., Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2023;57(6):306–314, section 'Fasciotomies': 'Most authors suggest that fasciotomies should be undertaken only when clearly indicated, based on clinical conditions (absence of distal pulses due to compression, more than expected pain due to an injured limb, or the need for radical debridement of necrotic muscle mass) or objective measurements of intracompartmental pressure. The latter include compartmental pressures in the range of 30-40 mm Hg, especially if there is no trend to decrease within a 6-hour interval.' — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10837607/

issues.step: Crush: after extrication and in hospital
issues.claim: StepDose("Children — isotonic saline after extrication, none given before (ISN RDRTF)", WeightDose(15.0, 20.0, unit = "mL", per = "per hour, IV isotonic saline"), note = "Adults 1,000 mL/h (RMMJ 2011); once 6 L has been given, evaluate urine output and volume status")
issues.problem: Nothing caps the calculator. Above about 50 kg it shows more than the adult rate that the same source gives (70 kg gives 1,050–1,400 mL/h, against 1,000 mL/h for adults). The note also applies the adult '6 L' reassessment point to the children's dose without saying it is an adult figure. The source gives the per-kg rate only for children and a fixed 1,000 mL/h for adults. It states no explicit cap, so the cap below is inferred from that adult figure.
issues.correction: Add maxTotal = 1000.0 (the RMMJ adult rate), or label the dose 'children (<50 kg)'. Reword the note: 'Adults 1,000 mL/h (RMMJ 2011). RMMJ: once the victim has received 6 L (adult figure), evaluate urine output and volume status; in children, reassess against weight and urine output.'
issues.evidence: Sever MS, Vanholder R. RMMJ 2011;2(2):e0039, 'Prophylaxis and treatment': 'If no intravenous fluid had been given prior to rescue, isotonic saline at a rate of 1,000 mL/h for adults (15–20 mL/kg/h for children) should be initiated. Once the victim has received 6 L of fluid, either before or after extrication, urine output and volume status should be evaluated' — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3678930/
